run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-15T09:12:49Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by a checkout rollout that broke checkout, which made frontend's /api/checkout return HTTP 500 through the proxy. At 09:21:27-09:21:30Z the checkout Deployment rolled from ReplicaSet checkout-5dccddf8bb (KAFKA_ADDR=kafka:9092, same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-checkout) to checkout-849d65649b (KAFKA_ADDR=kafka:9999); the kafka Service exposes only plaintext 9092 and controller 9093, and the new checkout container logs 'Failed to connect to broker kafka:9999: dial tcp 100.66.162.182:9999: i/o timeout', terminates with reason Error/exitCode 2, is never Ready (ContainersNotReady, BackOff event) and leaves the checkout Service with zero endpoints. frontend then fails its grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder calls (plus tcp.connect errors) and answers /api/checkout with 500, visible in frontend-proxy access logs as 'POST /api/checkout HTTP/1.1" 500 - via_upstream ... frontend', which the proxy's ingress and 'router frontend egress' spans record as STATUS_CODE_ERROR: proxy error spans rise from a steady 1-5 per 5m (09:05-09:26) to 66.7, 227.8, 397.8, 378.9, 394.4, 252.1, 95.9 per 5m, and over the 12m to 09:36:51 ingress errors were 236.6 and egress errors 235.5, matching frontend's 235.5 failed /api/checkout requests. Frontend error spans were exactly 0 before the rollout and only checkout-related operations fail; frontend, frontend-proxy and kafka pods are Running/Ready with 0 restarts. A separate, much smaller pre-existing 503 mode (Envoy 'UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' from frontend, 1-5 errors per 5m from ~09:05, before the checkout pod existed at 09:21) is the only evidence predating the alert start and its root cause is unknown.

claims.text: frontend-proxy records its own error spans on both 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress' with status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR; over the 12 minutes ending 09:36:51Z that was 236.58 ingress error spans and 235.50 egress error spans, against 1677-1821 non-error ingress/egress spans per 2m point earlier in the window.

The frontend-proxy error rate was low and steady before ~09:26Z (1.11, 3.33, 5.00, 4.67, 4.44, 1.09, 4.44, 5.56, 5.56 errors per 5m from 09:05 to ~09:26) and then jumped sharply: 66.67 (window ending 09:26:20Z), 227.78, 397.78, 378.89, 394.44, 252.10, 95.88 per 5m at the last (partial) point.

frontend has its own STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans and they are exclusively checkout-related: over the 12m ending 09:36:51Z the error increases were POST (235.50), POST /api/checkout (235.50), 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' (235.50) and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (235.50), plus tcp.connect (23.77); every other frontend span name (GET, GET /api/cart, GET /api/data, POST /api/cart, 'executing api route (pages) /api/cart', 'executing api route (pages) /api/data', grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart) showed 0 in that window.

frontend error spans were exactly 0 in every 5m window from 09:05Z until the window ending 09:26:20Z, where they first appear (125.56), then 458.89, 820, 767.78, 812.22, 514.20, 189.11 per 5m; frontend-proxy errors over the 12m to 09:36:51 (472.09 total: 236.58 ingress + 235.50 egress) match frontend's 235.5 failed checkout requests rather than being an independent proxy fault.

frontend-proxy access logs (window 09:26:00-09:29:54Z) contain 140 responses with a 5xx status; the 60 newest (09:28:32-09:29:53Z) are all 'POST /api/checkout HTTP/1.1" 500 - via_upstream ... frontend', e.g. 'POST /api/checkout HTTP/1.1" 500 - via_upstream - "-" 380 21 303 303 ... frontend 100.96.4.193:43896 ...' at 09:28:32.644Z, i.e. the 500 came from the frontend upstream, not from the proxy itself.

Only one of the 140 frontend-proxy 5xx lines in 09:26-09:29:54Z was a 503: 'GET /api/cart HTTP/1.1" 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' to upstream frontend at 09:27:25.501Z; the earlier error traces (09:01:22-09:08:18Z sample) show the same 503 pattern - frontend-proxy ingress with http.status_code 503 / otel.status_code ERROR plus a 'router frontend egress' span with error="true" http.status_code="0", and the whole trace of 6fa8d953d64adf50d2609c4b5715a54c contains only load-generator and frontend-proxy spans (no frontend span).

Kubernetes events show a checkout Deployment rollout at 09:21:27-09:21:30Z: 'Scaled up replica set checkout-849d65649b from 0 to 1', 'Scaled down replica set checkout-5dccddf8bb from 1 to 0', 'SuccessfulDelete ... Deleted pod: checkout-5dccddf8bb-9d9c8', Scheduled/Created checkout-849d65649b-qqtsz, and a later Warning BackOff 'Back-off restarting failed container checkout in pod checkout-849d65649b-qqtsz_otel-demo' at 09:28:33Z.

The two checkout ReplicaSets differ only in the KAFKA_ADDR value (same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-checkout): checkout-5dccddf8bb (owner Deployment/checkout, replicas 0) has KAFKA_ADDR=kafka:9092, while checkout-849d65649b (owner Deployment/checkout, replicas 1) has KAFKA_ADDR=kafka:9999; the live checkout Deployment template now carries KAFKA_ADDR=kafka:9999.

The kafka Service in otel-demo exposes only ports plaintext 9092 -> 9092 and controller 9093 -> 9093 (no 9999), and its endpoints are populated (address 100.96.4.148 with ports plaintext 9092 and controller 9093); the checkout Service endpoint set is empty (no addresses) on port 8080.

Pod checkout-849d65649b-qqtsz (owner ReplicaSet checkout-849d65649b, phase Running) is Ready=False with reason ContainersNotReady ('containers with unready status: [checkout]'); its checkout container is not ready/not started, restartCount 1, last termination reason Error exitCode 2 finished 09:25:05Z and current state terminated reason Error exitCode 2 finished 09:28:32Z; init container wait-for-kafka Completed with exitCode 0 at 09:21:29Z.

The checkout container logs repeat 'Failed to connect to broker kafka:9999: dial tcp 100.66.162.182:9999: i/o timeout' and 'client/metadata got error from broker -1 while fetching metadata: dial tcp 100.66.162.182:9999: i/o timeout' roughly every 30s from 09:21:59Z through 09:29:47Z, with 'starting to listen on tcp: "[::]:8080"' logged at 09:23:30Z and 09:27:07Z.

checkout trace activity existed before the rollout and then stopped: checkout span increases (all STATUS_CODE_UNSET) were 3069.91 in the 12m ending 09:28:51Z (covering from 09:16:51Z), 1407.32, 853.21, then 0 in the 12m ending 09:34:51Z and 09:36:51Z, consistent with the service losing all endpoints; over the 12m ending 09:36:51Z only frontend (965.78) and frontend-proxy (472.09) returned STATUS_CODE_ERROR increases, while accounting, ad, fraud-detection, payment and recommendation returned 0.

Checked and healthy: pods frontend-675fd7b5c5-n4sbv and frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-h7j7c are Running with ready=true and restartCount 0, startup 2026-11-15T08:48:08Z; Deployments frontend and frontend-proxy report ready 1 / available 1 / unavailable <none>; kafka-ff7884766-ntckh is Running ready with 0 restarts.

Primary cause: the checkout Deployment was changed at ~09:21Z to KAFKA_ADDR=kafka:9999, a port the kafka Service does not expose (9092/9093 only). The checkout container cannot reach a broker on that port (i/o timeout to 100.66.162.182:9999), exits with reason Error/exitCode 2 and never becomes Ready, so the checkout Service has no endpoints; frontend's PlaceOrder calls fail (tcp.connect error spans) and frontend answers /api/checkout with HTTP 500, which frontend-proxy records as ingress/egress STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans, driving RequestErrorRate above 0 for frontend-proxy.

Secondary, separate cause with unknown root: a low-rate 503 mode existed before the checkout rollout - Envoy response flag 'UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' with upstream frontend, giving frontend-proxy 1-5 error spans per 5m from ~09:05Z to ~09:26Z and 503 error traces at 09:01:22-09:08:18Z; because this predates the checkout pod (created 09:21:27Z) it is the only proxy-error evidence available for the alert's 09:12:49Z start, but its trigger (e.g. frontend resetting connections) is not established by the evidence.

Rejected: frontend-proxy itself failing as the source of the errors. Its pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-h7j7c is Running/Ready with 0 restarts, its Deployment shows ready 1 / available 1, and its access logs show the failing responses were produced by the frontend upstream ('500 - via_upstream ... frontend'), so the proxy is relaying an upstream failure rather than generating it.

Rejected: a Kafka broker outage as the cause. Pod kafka-ff7884766-ntckh is Running, Ready and has 0 restarts, the kafka Service has a populated endpoint (100.96.4.148) on plaintext 9092 and controller 9093, and the checkout error text names port 9999 specifically ('dial tcp 100.66.162.182:9999: i/o timeout'), i.e. a port the Service does not publish, not the broker's 9092 listener.

gaps: The alerting rule itself is not visible: list_prometheus_rules returned no rule named RequestErrorRate and no rule carrying label service_name="frontend-proxy", so the alert expression and the reported 'current: 1.7333333333333332' value cannot be tied to a specific metric or unit.

Frontend application logs could not be read: fetch_pod_logs for frontend-675fd7b5c5-n4sbv returned 0 lines / 0 bytes for both filtered and unfiltered queries in 09:20-09:36Z, so the frontend-side error text for /api/checkout is unverified apart from its error spans.

Kafka container logs were readable (1500 lines) but none matched 9092|9093|listener|started, so Kafka's own listener configuration cannot be confirmed from logs; kafka health is asserted only from pod Ready status, 0 restarts and populated endpoints.

The change-history integration is not available in this Run, so who/how/when changed checkout KAFKA_ADDR to kafka:9999 is known only through the rollout events at 09:21:27-09:21:30Z and the ReplicaSet templates.
checkout's previous container instance logs were reported unavailable ('previous terminated container not found'), so the earlier (KAFKA_ADDR=kafka:9092) container's behavior cannot be inspected.

Jaeger trace data lagged (data_as_of about 09:08Z for the error-trace search and no traces returned for 09:25-09:36Z), so no error traces exist for the peak of the incident and the span-level view of the checkout-lost 500s is not available.

Services cart, checkout, currency, email, product-catalog, quote, shipping, load-generator, image-provider and kafka returned no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series in the 12m window, which is unknown rather than zero; only accounting, ad, fraud-detection, payment and recommendation returned an explicit 0.

Downstream/customer impact is not directly measured: load-generator error spans with http.status_code 503 were only sampled at 09:01-09:08Z (the earlier 503 mode), and no load-generator evidence for the checkout-induced 500s was retrieved.
next_steps: Set checkout's KAFKA_ADDR back to kafka:9092 (the value held by the previous ReplicaSet checkout-5dccddf8bb) and roll the Deployment, then confirm checkout-* becomes Ready and the checkout Service gains an endpoint and that frontend /api/checkout stops returning 500.
Review the change that set KAFKA_ADDR=kafka:9999 in the checkout Deployment at ~09:21Z through the cluster's change history/GitOps source, since the change-history integration was not queryable here.

Once the alerting rule is available in Prometheus, check the RequestErrorRate expression to confirm whether it counts frontend-proxy ingress 5xx spans and whether the pre-existing low-rate 503 mode alone (before 09:21Z) was already enough to trip the '> 0' threshold.

Investigate the separate frontend upstream resets ('UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' on GET /api/cart, 1-5 per 5m since ~09:05Z) using frontend-side metrics/logs, as they are a second, unexplained error source on the same proxy.
Verify kafka's plaintext 9092 listener configuration directly (broker logs or a connectivity probe from a checkout pod) to close the one unverified link in the chain.

view.cannot_prove: Only what the containers wrote to standard output and standard error and the node still keeps: the current instance and the one before it, nothing older and nothing from a pod that no longer exists. No matching line is not proof that something did not happen; lines cut by limit or by the read limit, and lines not read, are unknown, not absent.

Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). <none> means the path reached no value in that object, not that the field is absent from the kind; a filtered table is not a full picture of the kind.
